title: io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks extension (SEP-2663, released 2026-07-28) - the pin ghantika's Tasks-extension adapter is checked against
description: Vendored, in-repo pin (never an npm dependency - no io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks package exists to depend on) of the RELEASED SEP-2663 contract itself, not our own emitted shape. Before story-0137 this file documented what src/tasksAdapter.ts happened to return; tasksAdapter.ts's own header discloses it was designed before finalization and never reconciled, so that earlier version pinned our own pre-finalization guess, not the spec. This version pins the spec's actual field names, discriminated status variants, and request/response shapes; scripts/check-sdk-exact-pin.mjs's schema-vs-implementation check is what now verifies our adapter conforms TO this pin, rather than this pin describing the adapter. config/tasks-schema-digest.json records this file's SHA-256 so drift between the two is caught, not silently trusted. Every variant below restates its own fields in full rather than composing a shared base via `allOf` or `$ref`-plus-siblings: test/tasks.test.ts's hand-rolled validator implements only the keyword set this schema actually needs, `allOf` deliberately not among them (extending it is test-infrastructure work this repo has been directed to stop), and that same validator resolves a `$ref` by replacing the node it appears on, so a `$ref` next to sibling properties would silently validate nothing. The duplication below is the honest cost of staying inside that validator's real behavior.

taskStatus.description: The spec's closed, five-value status enum. ghantika only ever EMITS four of these ('working', 'completed', 'failed', 'cancelled') - see emittedTaskStatus below for that narrower, honestly-reachable set. 'input_required' is a legal spec value this schema must accept (a conformant client cannot assume it never appears from a Tasks-capable server in general), but it is structurally unreachable from ghantika specifically: a job-backed task has no client-input step, so ghantika's own adapter never constructs an InputRequiredTask.

emittedTaskStatus.description: The subset of taskStatus ghantika's adapter actually produces. A deep-equals against the full taskStatus enum above is not a valid conformance check once this schema pins the spec's five values - test/tasks.test.ts asserts this set is a SUBSET of taskStatus.enum, not equal to it, and states why 'input_required' is excluded (structurally unreachable, not merely unobserved).

taskOutputCounts.description: The backing job's real, ever-cumulative output volume (never decremented by retention eviction). ghantika's own extension of the spec's free-form CompletedTask.result / FailedTask.error JSONObject, not a spec-defined field name itself.

watchStoppedInfo.description: Present once this adapter's own output-driven notification WATCH (the wake accelerator - see notifications/tasks/status) has auto-stopped early - currently only ever for a sustained firehose rate. Never means the backing job stopped. ghantika's own extension of the spec's free-form result/error JSONObject on a TERMINAL task; see this schema's header note on the still-open pre-terminal placement question for a still-'working' task whose watch stopped early - flagged to the Manager rather than silently resolved here.

ghantikaResultExtras.description: ghantika's own additions inside the spec's free-form CompletedTask.result / FailedTask.error JSONObject - never top-level Task fields, since the spec's base Task/WorkingTask/CancelledTask interfaces carry no such container and a1 requires every top-level field we emit to be one the spec defines.

workingTask.description: The spec's WorkingTask: Task's base fields, status pinned to 'working', no result/error - restated in full rather than composed, see this schema's header.

completedTask.description: The spec's CompletedTask: Task's base fields, status pinned to 'completed', plus the spec's free-form result JSONObject (ghantika's own exitCode/output/watchStopped live inside it, see ghantikaResultExtras) - restated in full rather than composed, see this schema's header.

failedTask.description: The spec's FailedTask: Task's base fields, status pinned to 'failed', plus the spec's free-form error JSONObject (ghantika's own exitCode/output/watchStopped live inside it, see ghantikaResultExtras) - restated in full rather than composed, see this schema's header.

cancelledTask.description: The spec's CancelledTask: Task's base fields, status pinned to 'cancelled', no result/error - restated in full rather than composed, see this schema's header.

detailedTask.description: The spec's DetailedTask discriminated union, narrowed to the four variants ghantika's job model can ever actually produce (working / completed / failed / cancelled - never input_required). A pure oneOf of bare $refs - no siblings alongside either $ref, which is the one form this repo's hand-rolled validator resolves correctly.

createTaskResult.description: CreateTaskResult = Result & Task per the spec: the flat base-Task shape (never a DetailedTask variant - a freshly minted task carries no result/error yet even if the backing job happened to already be terminal at mint time), with resultType:'task' replacing the normal CallToolResult content/structuredContent shape. Returned by run() on a Tasks-capable connection - see this schema's header note on the still-unconfirmed wire mechanics of this replacement. Restated in full rather than composed, see this schema's top-level header.

getTaskResultWorking.description: GetTaskResult's 'working' branch: WorkingTask's fields plus resultType:'complete', restated in full - see getTaskResult below.

getTaskResultCompleted.description: GetTaskResult's 'completed' branch: CompletedTask's fields plus resultType:'complete', restated in full - see getTaskResult below.

getTaskResultFailed.description: GetTaskResult's 'failed' branch: FailedTask's fields plus resultType:'complete', restated in full - see getTaskResult below.

getTaskResultCancelled.description: GetTaskResult's 'cancelled' branch: CancelledTask's fields plus resultType:'complete', restated in full - see getTaskResult below.

getTaskResult.description: GetTaskResult = Result & DetailedTask per the spec: resultType:'complete' flattened alongside whichever DetailedTask variant matches the task's current status. Returned by tasks/get (and, in ghantika's own design, also by tasks/update - see ackResult for the spec-defined tasks/update shape this schema does NOT use). A pure oneOf of bare $refs to the four resultType-carrying variants above, each already self-contained - never composed via allOf or $ref-plus-siblings, see this schema's top-level header.

ackResult.description: UpdateTaskResult / CancelTaskResult per the spec: an empty acknowledgement carrying only resultType:'complete', nothing else. Both are eventually-consistent per the spec - the ack may arrive before the task's observable status reflects the requested change.

taskNotFoundError.description: Not a success-result shape at all. The spec answers an unknown OR an expired-and-purged taskId with the same JSON-RPC error code (-32602, Invalid params) - it does not differentiate the two at the protocol level, so ghantika's prior tagged-success taskNotFound shape is retired: tasks/get, tasks/update, and tasks/cancel alike now THROW rather than returning a value shaped like this. Kept here only as documentation of the error code this schema's consumers must expect, not as a schema any response is validated against.
